result: In cellular rootlets (partially purified, membrane-associated), cryo-ET revealed flexible protrusions emanating from cross-striations that connect to intracellular membranes. Segmentation showed perpendicular densities weaving between longitudinal filaments, forming an intricate network. These protrusions contacted membranes directly or via ~7 nm globular membrane-associated densities covering membrane surfaces.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praised the study for revealing membrane connections, stating 'they observed striations along the membranes along the rootlet' and noting the 'exceptional' micrographs with 'excellent contrast and details.' No concerns were raised about these cellular observations.

result: In purified rootlets, striations were classified into two discrete D-bands (D1 and D2) and one amorphous A-band per 80.1 nm repeat. D1 is closest to the centriole and A-band to the tip, establishing a polar arrangement. The D1-D2 spacing is 23.9 nm, D2-A is 18.0 nm, and A-D1 (next repeat) is 38.1 nm. This classification and repeat distance are consistent with prior EM measurements.
evaluation: Reviewers highlighted that the authors 'described how the cross-striations form 3 types of periodic structures -D1/D2/A bands-' as a key finding. They noted this delivers 'an unprecedented level of resolution' and that 'previous work did not identify the two distinct types,' affirming the novelty and acceptance of this classification.

result: D-bands span the rootlet interior, embedded within longitudinal filaments. They consist of punctate densities associated with filaments that laterally connect via thin protrusions, suggesting they bundle rootlet filaments. Rootlets can splay into sub-fibers with D1-D1 alignment (22/48 cases), D1-D2 alignment (17/48), or no alignment (9/48), raising the possibility that D1 and D2 have the same composition.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the study's description of how striations are 'connected perpendicularly to filaments along the length of the rootlets,' and praised the 'state-of-the-art cryo-electron tomography' and 'image analysis' that enabled these observations. No critiques were raised about the D-band structural characterization.

result: A-bands contain lateral connections that are fuzzier and broader than D-bands. Large amorphous accumulations on the rootlet surface align with A-bands and show evidence of connecting to them. These surface densities were absent in cellular rootlets, suggesting they accumulate during purification, possibly from membrane-associated proteins aggregating upon membrane removal.
evaluation: Reviewers noted the authors' observation of 'striations along the membranes' and did not question the interpretation that surface accumulations are purification artifacts. The overall model of A-band structure and membrane connections was accepted as part of the 'detailed model for the molecular organization of the rootlet.'

result: Fourier analysis showed strong longitudinal peaks but no lateral peaks, indicating longitudinal filaments are not in a regular array. Segmentation revealed filaments run in similar but not strictly parallel directions. Two filament types were observed: thicker (~5 nm) and thinner, more flexible filaments. Thick filaments can 'melt' locally or splay into thin filaments that merge with others, indicating flexible association.
evaluation: Reviewers praised the 'state-of-the-art cryo-electron tomography, sub-tomogram averaging, and image analysis' and noted the study's success in revealing the 'highly flexible network of filaments.' No concerns were raised about the filament heterogeneity or flexibility observations.

result: Subtomogram averaging of 180,252 particles (from 591,453 extracted) revealed filaments consist of two intertwined coiled coils. Classification showed a helical groove along the filament, and fitting crystal structures (tropomyosin, lamin, rootletin CC3) confirmed dimensions consistent with two intertwined coiled-coil dimers. The oligomerization interface extends ~50 nm. AlphaFold2 predicted rootletin as a coiled coil (~265 nm long), including the N-terminus previously thought globular.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly commended the 'high-quality study' using 'state-of-the-art cryo-electron tomography, sub-tomogram averaging, and image analysis.' They noted the 'exceptional' micrographs and did not raise concerns about the subtomogram averaging or structural modeling, affirming the conclusion that filaments are pairs of coiled coils.

result: The authors propose a model where thick filaments are parallel bundles of rootletin coiled-coil pairs. Rootletin coiled coils form paired bundles between CC2-CC4 but separate in CC1 regions. The 80.1 nm repeat is shorter than rootletin's ~265 nm length, suggesting an 80.1 nm staggered alignment of rootletin molecules. Weak interactions between offset coiled coils require intermediary proteins. A parallel (not antiparallel) orientation accounts for the asymmetric striation pattern.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the study provides 'a compelling molecular model for the organization of rootlets' and 'a detailed model for the molecular organization of the rootlet.' They praised the 'unprecedented level of resolution' and did not challenge the proposed staggered, parallel model or the interpretation of rootletin organization.

result: The authors propose D-bands are formed by a protein other than rootletin that bundles rootletin into oligomers, with CEP68 and CCDC102B as candidates. The presence of two D-bands per repeat (vs. one rootletin N-terminus per repeat) suggests D-bands are not rootletin. Depletion studies and lack of interaction between CEP68 and CCDC102B suggest they form separate bundling connections. CCDC102B's extended morphology fits lateral connections between D-band puncta.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the overall model, stating the study provides 'a detailed model for the molecular organization of the rootlet.' They did not question the speculation about D-band composition or the candidacy of CEP68/CCDC102B, treating these as reasonable interpretations within the model.

result: The authors propose the rootletin N-terminus aligns with the A-band and contains putative membrane connection sites. Deletion of the N-terminus removed the prominent band in overexpression studies. Amorphous densities on purified rootlet surfaces (absent in cellular rootlets) may be aggregates of membrane-associated proteins at A-band membrane interaction sites. Candidates for membrane links include KLC3 and Nesprin1, which interact with the rootletin N-terminus.
evaluation: Reviewers noted the authors 'described how the cross-striations form 3 types of periodic structures... connected perpendicularly to filaments along the length of the rootlets and to membranes.' They accepted the model of A-band membrane connections without raising concerns, affirming this as part of the 'detailed model for the molecular organization of the rootlet.'

result: Rootlets do not form coherent round bundles but are often split, flattened, or surrounded by organelles. They can splay apart and rejoin, consistent with observed branching into sub-fibers and heterogeneity in classification. This flexibility may allow rootlets to extend between and tether organelles without restricting organelle shape. The rootlet is built of a highly flexible network of filaments connected by three types of cross-striation bands that protrude and connect to membranes.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the study reveals the rootlet as 'a highly flexible network of filaments connected by three types of cross-striation bands' and praised the 'unprecedented level of resolution.' They accepted the flexibility and functional implications without critique, treating this as a key advance in understanding rootlet organization.

result: Background and methodological claims establish that ciliary rootlets are striated bundles critical for cilia function, composed primarily of rootletin and other proteins (CEP68, CCDC102B, C-Nap1, Nesprin1α). Rootlets were isolated from mouse photoreceptor cells using established protocols, and purification methods (detergent extraction, vortexing) yielded clear rootlets suitable for cryo-EM/ET. Previous work did not identify the two distinct D-band and A-band types now reported.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the study's methodological rigor, noting 'the sample preparation was well optimized to provide excellent samples for cryo-ET' and that the manuscript is 'clear and accessible.' They accepted the background context and novelty claims, stating 'previous work did not identify the two distinct types' of striations.
